verses.zh: （大卫的诗，照耶杜顿的作法，交与伶长。）我的心默默无声，专等候　神；我的救恩是从他而来。
verses.en: For the music director, Jeduthun; a psalm of David.For God alone I patiently wait;[NOTE:1] he is the one who delivers me.[NOTE:2]
notes: Psalm 62. The psalmist expresses his unwavering confidence in God’s justice and in his ability to protect his people.
Heb “only for God [is] there silence [to] my soul.”

verses.zh: 惟独他是我的磐石，我的拯救；他是我的高台，我必不很动摇。
verses.en: He alone is my protector[NOTE:1] and deliverer.He is my refuge;[NOTE:2] I will not be upended.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “from him [is] my deliverance.”
Heb “my high rocky summit.”
Or “my elevated place” (see Ps 18:2).

verses.zh: 你们大家攻击一人，把他毁坏，如同毁坏歪斜的墙、将倒的壁，要到几时呢？
verses.en: How long will you threaten[NOTE:1] a man like me?All of you are murderers,[NOTE:2] as dangerous as a leaning wall or an unstable fence.[NOTE:3]
notes: The Hebrew text adds רַבָּה (rabbah, “greatly”) at the end of the line. It is unusual for this adverb to follow a negated verb. Some see this as qualifying the assertion to some degree, but this would water down the affirmation too much (see v. 6b, where the adverb is omitted). If the adverb has a qualifying function, it would suggest that the psalmist might be shaken, though not severely. This is inconsistent with the confident mood of the psalm. The adverb probably has an emphatic force here, “I will not be greatly shaken” meaning “I will not be upended.”

The verb form is plural; the psalmist addresses his enemies. The verb הוּת (hut) occurs only here in the OT. An Arabic cognate means “shout at.” Here “man” is a generic reference to the victim of the psalmist’s enemies, but in context it ultimately refers to the psalmist himself. To clarify this, the words “like me” have been supplied in the translation.
The Hebrew text has a Pual (passive) form, but the verb form should be vocalized as a Piel (active) form. See BDB 953-54 s.v. רָצַח.

verses.zh: 他们彼此商议，专要从他的尊位上把他推下；他们喜爱谎话，口虽祝福，心却咒诅。（细拉）
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] spend all their time planning how to bring their victim[NOTE:2] down.[NOTE:3] They love to use deceit;[NOTE:4] they pronounce blessings with their mouths,but inwardly they utter curses.[NOTE:5] (Selah)
notes: Heb “like a bent wall and a broken fence.” The point of the comparison is not entirely clear. Perhaps the enemies are depicted as dangerous, like a leaning wall or broken fence that is in danger of falling on someone (see C. A. Briggs and E. G. Briggs, Psalms [ICC], 2:69).
That is, the psalmist’s enemies addressed in the previous verse.
That is, the generic “man” referred to in the previous verse. The words “their victim” have been supplied in the translation to clarify the referent.
Heb “only from his lofty place [or perhaps, “dignity”] they plan to drive [him] away.”
Heb “they delight [in] a lie.”

verses.zh: 我的心哪，你当默默无声，专等候　神，因为我的盼望是从他而来。
verses.en: Patiently wait for God alone, my soul![NOTE:1] For he is the one who gives me hope.[NOTE:2]
notes: The enemies use deceit to bring down their victim. They make him think they are his friends by pronouncing blessings upon him, but inwardly they desire his demise.

Heb “only for God be silent, my soul.” The wording is similar to that of v. 1a. Here an imperatival form, דּוֹמִּי (dommi, “be silent”), appears instead of the noun דּוּמִיָּה (dumiyyah, “silence”). The psalmist is encouraging himself to maintain his trust in God.

verses.zh: 惟独他是我的磐石，我的拯救；他是我的高台，我必不动摇。
verses.en: He alone is my protector[NOTE:1] and deliverer.He is my refuge;[NOTE:2] I will not be shaken.
notes: Heb “for from him [is] my hope.”
Heb “my high rocky summit.”

verses.zh: 我的拯救、我的荣耀都在乎　神；我力量的磐石、我的避难所都在乎　神。
verses.en: God delivers me and exalts me;God is my strong protector and my shelter.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “my elevated place” (see Ps 18:2).

verses.zh: 你们众民当时时倚靠他，在他面前倾心吐意；　神是我们的避难所。（细拉）
verses.en: Trust in him at all times, you people!Pour out your hearts before him.[NOTE:1] God is our shelter. (Selah)
notes: Heb “upon God [is] my deliverance and my glory, the high rocky summit of my strength, my shelter [is] in God.”

verses.zh: 下流人真是虚空；上流人也是虚假；放在天平里就必浮起；他们一共比空气还轻。
verses.en: Men are nothing but a mere breath;human beings are unreliable.[NOTE:1] When they are weighed in the scales,all of them together are lighter than air.[NOTE:2]
notes: To “pour out one’s heart” means to offer up to God intense, emotional lamentation and petitionary prayers (see Lam 2:19).

Heb “only a breath [are] the sons of mankind, a lie [are] the sons of man.” The phrases “sons of mankind” and “sons of man” also appear together in Ps 49:2. Because of the parallel line there, where “rich and poor” are mentioned, a number of interpreters and translators treat these expressions as polar opposites, בְּנֵי אָדָם (bene ʾadam) referring to the lower classes and בְּנֵי אִישׁ (bene ʾish) to higher classes. But usage does not support such a view. The rare phrase בְּנֵי אִישׁ (“sons of man”) appears to refer to human beings in general in its other uses (see Pss 4:2; Lam 3:33). It is better to understand the phrases as synonymous expressions.

verses.zh: 不要仗势欺人，也不要因抢夺而骄傲；若财宝加增，不要放在心上。
verses.en: Do not trust in what you can gain by oppression.[NOTE:1] Do not put false confidence in what you can gain by robbery.[NOTE:2] If wealth increases, do not become attached to it.[NOTE:3]
notes: The noun הֶבֶל (hevel), translated “a breath” earlier in the verse, appears again here.
Heb “do not trust in oppression.” Here “oppression” stands by metonymy for the riches that can be gained by oppressive measures, as the final line of the verse indicates.
Heb “and in robbery do not place vain hope.” Here “robbery” stands by metonymy for the riches that can be gained by theft, as the next line of the verse indicates.

verses.zh: 神说了一次、两次，我都听见：就是能力都属乎　神。
verses.en: God has declared one principle;two principles I have heard:[NOTE:1] God is strong,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “[as for] wealth, when it bears fruit, do not set [your] heart [on it].”

Heb “one God spoke, two which I heard.” This is a numerical saying utilizing the “x” followed by “x + 1” pattern to facilitate poetic parallelism. (See W. M. W. Roth, Numerical Sayings in the Old Testament [VTSup], 55-56.) As is typical in such sayings, a list corresponding to the second number (in this case “two”) follows. Another option is to translate, “God has spoken once, twice [he has spoken] that which I have heard.” The terms אַחַת (ʾakhat, “one; once”) and שְׁתַיִם (shetayim, “two; twice”) are also juxtaposed in 2 Kgs 6:10 (where they refer to an action that was done more than “once or twice”) and in Job 33:14 (where they refer to God speaking “one way” and then in “another manner”).

verses.zh: 主啊，慈爱也是属乎你，因为你照着各人所行的报应他。
verses.en: and you, O Lord, demonstrate loyal love.[NOTE:1] For you repay men for what they do.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “that strength [belongs] to God.”
Heb “and to you, O Master, [is] loyal love.”
